A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable main text, Table 1, algorithm listings, proofs, and appendices. Material moved between the appendices and main text can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical algorithms and guarantees, including in its appendices, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes. Its empirical-risk results are mathematical guarantees.

after.justification: V2 remains a theoretical paper. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original empirical measurements.

M1.justification: V2 revises the single-pass algorithms' period and clipping-parameter prescriptions and corrects Algorithm 1's node-selection condition from k' <= k to k' <= t. The underlying O2NC framework and gradient-oracle constructions remain; the first-order algorithm already appeared in v1 Appendix B.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or concrete test scenarios. Both study the same abstract nonsmooth, nonconvex optimization problems.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Zhang et al. (2024) as the theoretical comparator. Neither version reports an experimentally evaluated baseline set, and the added citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental evaluation protocols, splits, metrics, or training budgets. Revisions to theoretical algorithm parameter prescriptions are covered under M1 and D1.

E4.justification: Neither version reports empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. The first-order analysis and optimal-smoothing extension already exist in v1; their relocation does not introduce supplementary experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The concentration results concern theoretical guarantees rather than uncertainty estimated from experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the single-pass sample-complexity expression 1/(αβ³) + d/(εαβ²) + d^(3/4)/(ε^(1/2)αβ^(5/2)) with sqrt(d)/(αβ³) + d/(εαβ²), suppressing the same factors. These are substantially revised theoretical results, not measured performance changes. The multi-pass entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 repairs the single-pass derivation by retaining L/sqrt(B1), hence L/sqrt(Σ), in Equation (9), where v1 mishandles and drops this contribution. Revised parameter choices yield corrected Theorems 3.1 and 6.1, the latter corresponding to v1 Theorem B.4. V2 also uses AM-GM to absorb the mixed term and corrects smaller indexing and variance-factor errors.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, Remark 3.2, and discussion replace the central claim of a dimension-independent non-private term with a sqrt(d)-dependent, sublinear term. This materially narrows the claimed guarantee. The Ω(sqrt(d)) improvement over Zhang et al. and the multi-pass contributions remain.

C2.justification: New Remark 3.3 discusses trading sample complexity against oracle complexity. Remark 6.2 additionally contrasts the retained first-order oracle saving with the smaller non-private oracle gap. Existing limitations concerning approximate versus Rényi privacy and unresolved lower bounds remain.

D1.justification: The explicit single-pass tuning prescriptions change: Σ gains an α/(D sqrt(d)) term, and D gains an additional dimension-dependent cap in Theorems 3.1 and 6.1. These revise documented algorithm settings; no code release, hardware information, or experimental implementation details are added.

R1.justification: V2 adds supporting references to Abadi et al., Kulkarni et al., LeCun et al., Keskar et al., and Villalobos et al., principally for privacy composition and motivation. The central relationship to Zhang et al. remains, with the novelty claim narrowed to sublinear dimension dependence. Grimmer and Jia's publication update is the same cited work.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: v1 Appendix B becomes Section 6 and Section 7.4, and the techniques explanation moves into a new introductory subsection. It also expands the introduction and tree-mechanism explanation and foregrounds the existing first-order contribution.

P2.justification: Both versions retain Table 1 and Algorithms 1–5. V2 lightly restyles the table, places Algorithms 1 and 2 together, moves Algorithm 5 into the main text, and reflows mathematical displays. There is no substantial addition or replacement of visual content.

improvement.justification: V2 resolves an important deficiency in a central guarantee: it restores the omitted variance contribution, revises the parameter choices and bounds, and withdraws the unsupported dimension-independent claim. Although the corrected guarantee is less ambitious, these changes substantially improve the paper's internal consistency and reliability. The pseudocode correction and clearer organization provide additional benefits.
